plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant, evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and in large fields for essential oil production and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to mid-summer (peak June to July in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the Romans added it to their bathwater, which is the origin of its name from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flower heads, composed of sterile sepals, set against broad glossy green leaves. It thrives in partial shade and moist soil.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in temperate gardens in Europe, North America, the Azores, and East Asia
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round, water-repellent leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. It grows in shallow ponds, lakes, and slow-moving waters.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in India, China, Vietnam, Japan, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that makes them self-cleaning, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that has inspired water-repellent materials.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, featuring a large bowl-shaped crown of pointed pink bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy flowers. It grows in fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor, acidic soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early summer, with many blooms in the Southern Hemisphere winter (May to September)
plants.location: South Africa's Western and Eastern Cape fynbos regions
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and it is adapted to wildfires, with underground lignotubers that resprout after burns.
